item: Hourly DNI, GHI, air temperature, humidity, wind
source: NASA POWER hourly API (power.larc.nasa.gov), community RE
validity_note: Satellite/model-derived, not ground-measured. Accuracy for Egypt/MENA not yet checked. Timestamps believed to be UTC - confirm before hourly dispatch.

item: Annual irradiation = sum of hourly DNI / 1000
source: Arithmetic (hourly W/m2 treated as Wh/m2 per hour)
validity_note: Assumes hourly average values.

item: Water / steam enthalpy h(p,T)
validity_note: Confirm which steam-table standard it implements and its validity range before citing.

item: Heat duty Q = m x (h_steam - h_feedwater)
validity_note: Heat carried by the steam. Ignores boiler efficiency, blowdown and condensate return; it is not the fuel input.

item: Annual demand = MW x hours/day x days/year
validity_note: Assumes constant load while the plant operates.

item: Preset city coordinates
validity_note: Good to about 0.1 deg. Use Coordinates mode for a specific plant.
status: Manual entry - fine for site selection

item: Solar field optical/thermal efficiency
validity_note: Gamil 2023 gives receiver efficiency for water at 50-150 C only. Heliostat-field efficiency depends on site and layout (see D8).
status: PARTLY - see D3 (receiver, water 50-150 C); field efficiency needs a layout model

item: Storage efficiency / heat loss
validity_note: Gamil 2023 assumes storage efficiency 1 (no loss). Old files used 0.85, 0.938 and 0.95 with no source.
status: PARTLY - no storage loss (Gamil 2023); see H4

item: Heliostat, receiver and tank costs
validity_note: Old app hard-coded 110 USD/m2, 1.2 M USD, 1200 USD/m3 with no source.
status: PARTLY - see E1, E2 (US small tower costs, to be replaced)

item: Discount rate, lifetime, O&M, fuel escalation
validity_note: Must be user inputs with a sourced default.
status: PARTLY - see E4 (derived from Gamil 2024, Table 5)

item: Soiling parameter (mu tilde)
validity_note: Needs local reflectance and PM10 calibration; will be a flagged estimate.
status: PARTLY - engine added (R1-R3); mu still needs local calibration

item: Nanofluid cp enhancement factors
validity_note: Old app used 0.05 / 0.08 / 0.12 per vol-% with no source.

item: Solar multiple SM = (t_TES + X) / X
validity_note: The source prints SM 1.3 and Eq. 2 gives 1.33, but its own receiver area (6.873 m2) implies about 1.36. Tool uses Eq. 2.

item: Receiver incident power Q_th,rec = Q_load x SM / (eta_rec x eta_pipe)
validity_note: Piping and tank heat losses are ignored by the source (eta_pipe = 1).

item: Receiver thermal efficiency 0.8589
validity_note: Tucson, stainless steel 316 + Pyromark, water 50-150 C, 40 m tower. Changes with wind, tube thickness and site (Fig. 16).

item: Allowable flux = q_limit / R_peak,avg ; q_limit 600 kW/m2 (SS316, water); R_peak,avg 2
source: Gamil 2023, Eq. 7 and p. 6 (q_limit cited from Armijo and Shinde 2016)
validity_note: The source explores R_peak,avg from 1.5 to 3 and picks 2 as a conservative value.

item: Receiver area, height and diameter (aspect ratio 1.5)
validity_note: Reproduces the paper's Table 6 geometry (6.873 m2, 1.811 m, 1.208 m) to 0.2 percent. Checked by a test.

item: Storage: fluid mass = Q_htf x t / (cp x dT); tank volume = mass / density
validity_note: Storage efficiency taken as 1 (no heat loss). Our check gives about 47 m3 against 50.6 m3 in Table 6 (-7 percent); the source used its own property correlations.

item: Liquid water cp and density at the average fluid temperature
validity_note: The source used Popiel and Wojtkowiak (1998) correlations for 0-150 C; the difference was not checked.

item: Heliostat field area = Q_th,rec / (DNI x eta_optical,DP); eta_optical,DP default 0.8412
source: Gamil 2023, Eq. 34-35; default value derived by us
validity_note: 0.8412 is NOT printed in the source. It is derived from 645 heliostats x 4 m2, DNI 950 W/m2 and Q_th,rec 2.062 MW (Tucson, 40 m tower, biomimetic layout). It depends on latitude, tower height and layout, so replace it for other sites.
status: Derived - site specific, must be replaced for other sites

item: Design DNI 950 W/m2; heliostat 2 x 2 m; sunlight hours X = 9; storage 3 h; fluid 50 to 150 C; 6 bar
validity_note: Defaults from the Tucson reference case only; the user can change them.

item: Validity range of the design method
validity_note: Pressurized liquid water to about 150 C. Not valid for 200 C steam or molten salt.
status: Scope limit - warnings shown in the app

item: Soiling model: reflectance = rho0 x (1 - soiled area x h(incidence angle)); h = 2 / cos(angle) for second-surface mirrors
validity_note: Validated on heliostats at 3 Australian sites only. NOT validated for Egypt or for trough collectors.
status: Source identified - validity to verify locally

item: Dust deposition per hour = PM10 x cos(mirror tilt) x mu
validity_note: mu is per time step; the app uses 1 hour. Rolling-off removal is absorbed inside mu; rain and humidity are not modelled.

item: mu = 4e-6 and sigma_dep = 1.5e-6 per hour
source: Example values from the soiling tool's synthetic demo
validity_note: NOT measured. They must come from a local reflectance campaign plus local PM10 data (fit with the tool's calibration).

item: PM10 dust level (constant or hourly CSV)
validity_note: The weather data we load has no PM10. A constant level ignores dust storms.

item: Cleaning: limit on reflectance reading (default 0.80) or fixed schedule; effectiveness 0.99
source: Pappa et al. 2025 (limit 0.8); Anderson et al. 2023 Table 3 (0.99)
validity_note: The limit is an operating choice that depends on cleaning cost and heat value. Pappa 2025 was listed as experimental in the tool.

item: Sun position and heliostat tilt / incidence angle
source: Duffie and Beckman (sun position); mirror normal bisects sun and receiver directions
validity_note: Standard geometry with no empirical parameters. Weather timestamps are assumed to be UTC (to confirm).

item: Field represented by mirrors on a ring around the tower; mirrors face down at night
validity_note: Not from the source papers. They affect the result (a face-up night position collects dust).

item: Clean mirror reflectance 0.88
source: Gamil, Li, Khammash 2023, text after Eq. 42
validity_note: Design value in the tower paper. Replace with the measured clean-mirror reflectance (measured at 15 degrees).

item: Hourly solar heat = DNI x field area x optical efficiency x mirror reflectance x receiver efficiency x availability
source: Anderson et al. 2023, Eq. 28-30 (as in the soiling tool); efficiencies from Gamil 2023 / 2024
validity_note: Optical efficiency must exclude reflectance so it is not counted twice: the app divides the source value by 0.88.
status: Source identified - structure from the tool, values from Gamil

item: Field optical efficiency 0.7997 (annual, weighted by sunlight); reflectivity inside it 0.88
source: Gamil, Li, Khammash 2023, Table 7 and text after Eq. 42
validity_note: Tucson, 40 m tower, biomimetic layout. A constant annual value flattens the daily shape; it depends on site, tower height and layout.
status: Source identified - site specific, constant-value simplification

item: Receiver efficiency 0.8098 (annual average); availability 0.96
source: Gamil, Li, Ali, Khammash 2024, Table 8 and Table 3
validity_note: Receiver efficiency really falls at low solar flux (Gamil 2023, Fig. 18); the constant value ignores that.

item: Storage dispatch: surplus charges storage, storage covers the shortfall, excess is not used
source: Anderson et al. 2023, Eq. 24-26 (as adapted in the soiling tool: plant demand replaces power-block demand)
validity_note: Storage capacity = fluid heat power x storage hours (the same basis as the tank size). No storage or piping loss, as in Gamil 2023.
status: Source identified - adaptation of the tool

item: Heat demand profile: constant load during the operating window, operating days spread evenly through the year
validity_note: Real plants have varying load. User sets hours per day, days per year and start hour.

item: Local time: weather hours are UTC; user gives the time zone
validity_note: To confirm in the NASA POWER documentation. A wrong assumption shifts the daily pattern by hours.

item: Validation case: Tucson, Arizona, about 5.6 GWh of solar heat produced per year
validity_note: The source used a typical meteorological year (NSRDB), we use one actual year from NASA POWER. To be run by the user and the result recorded.

item: Investment = heliostat field 75 USD/m2 + site preparation 15 USD/m2 + tower 200 USD/m + receiver 65 USD/m2 + fluid 0.8 USD/m3 + storage; contingency 7 %; indirect 11 %
validity_note: Costs of a small relocatable tower in the USA (heliostats 75 USD/m2 are industry figures from the authors' collaboration). Taken as printed, Table 4 adds up to about 286 000 USD, not the paper's total of 365 521 USD.
status: Source identified - discrepancy noted, replace with quotes

item: Thermal storage cost: default 32 USD per kWh of heat
source: Gamil 2024, Table B.2 (Fresnel plant); Table 4 prints 0.004 USD/kWh
validity_note: The printed 0.004 USD/kWh would make a whole storage system cost about 20 USD, so it looks like a unit error. 32 USD/kWh is the same paper's value for another plant. Our choice, not a measured water-tank cost.

item: Levelized cost of heat = (capital recovery factor x investment + O&M + cleaning) / heat delivered to the process
source: Standard capital-recovery method, written out in this tool
validity_note: The source's own LCOH (fixed charge rate method, 2.42 cents/kWh) could not be reproduced from its printed numbers (we get 1.24), so it is not used as a target. We divide by delivered heat, not heat produced.

item: Discount rate 5.31 % (real) and lifetime 20 years
source: Derived from Gamil 2024, Table 5 (50 % debt at 4 %, 13 % equity return, 28 % tax, 2.5 % inflation)
validity_note: Reproduces the paper's capital recovery factor 0.131 for 10 years. Taxes, depreciation and loans are not modelled separately. The paper uses 10 years for the relocatable plant and 20 years for the comparison plants.

item: Operation and maintenance 1.6 % of investment per year
validity_note: The source also has a variable operating cost that is not reported.

item: Fuel price 0.027 USD per kWh of fuel; boiler efficiency 0.80; CO2 0.198 kg per kWh of fuel
source: Gamil 2024, p. 12 (Arizona industrial gas 2022) and Eq. 9 / Table 6
validity_note: The price is for Arizona, NOT Egypt: replace it. The paper's own fuel and CO2 totals leave out the boiler efficiency; this tool includes it (heat / efficiency).
status: Source identified - price must be replaced

item: Cleaning cost per m2 of mirror per cleaning: default 0
source: User input (structure after Anderson et al. 2023, Eq. 20-22)
validity_note: No default is offered because none is sourced. With 0 the cleaning cost is ignored.

item: Cash flow: yearly fuel saving minus O&M and cleaning; no tax, subsidy, loan or degradation
validity_note: Heat delivered by the one-year simulation is repeated every year.
